name: Mrs. P. Malloy
role: Widow who ran the Western House and a Main Street hotel
bio: Mrs. P. Malloy kept running the Western House hotel after her husband's death, the paper reported in December 1884. In July 1885 she moved into a new hotel building put up for her on one of Joe Ferris' lots on Main Street, where she served suppers and held a dance. In June 1886 J. A. Ferris sued her for possession of property in Justice Copeland's court, and in July she moved to a cottage; by October another man was moving into the building she had occupied.

mentions: Mrs. Malloy is running the Western House in the same acceptable manner that it was before her husband's death.
Mrs. Malloy's sister, from Mankato, Minnesota, returned home Saturday after a short visit here.
Mrs. Malloy will soon occupy the building built for her on one of Joe Ferris' lots. Work has already begun on Joe's building which will be completed as soon as possible.
Mrs. Malloy moved yesterday from the Western house, to her new building on Main street. Supper was served at the new hotel last evening.
The dance at Mrs. Malloy's last night was a complete success. The owners of several sleepy looking pairs of eyes declared this morning that they wouldn't have missed it for a ranch.
Mrs. Molloy returned yesterday from a visit to Mr. and Mrs. Truscott's, at the Spring creek ranch.

In the case of J. A. Ferris vs. Mrs. P. Malloy, for possession of property, in Justice Copeland's court, the question of continuance is being argued as we go to press.
In Justice Copeland's court, the case of J. A. Ferris vs. Mrs. P. Malloy, which came up last Thursday, was postponed eight days.
Mrs. Malloy has moved to the cottage formerly occupied by D. O. Sweet. She still continues to take boarders.
